chapters.title: Install on Windows or Linux
chapters.description: Choose the right package and preserve your local store.

sections.title: Availability
sections.text: The current qualified local pair is Browser 0.4.10 and Workbench 0.5.15. Public source is available under the MIT license. Installers and native runtime binaries are not publicly distributed yet. There is no public download link to a tested binary release; use your locally built and verified artifacts. Installed desktop apps include their own Node runtime. Ordinary users do not need the Chromium source checkout.

sections.title: Windows x64
sections.text: Use the matching locally generated Browser NSIS .exe and its signed update manifest. Finish active work and use the tray menu’s Quit before replacing files. The accepted local upgrade uses an idle preflight and a fresh independently verified private backup; preserve that backup and its receipt. Browser 0.4.10 with the Workbench 0.5.15 add-on passed actual Windows installation and restart. A new standalone Workbench NSIS installation has not been qualified for this pair. Windows Authenticode publisher signing remains unconfigured.

sections.title: Linux x64 portable
sections.text: The qualified path is a per-user portable installation in an isolated Ubuntu account. Verify the archive against SHA256SUMS, extract it into a new directory, then run sh ./install.sh from that extracted product directory. The installer checks its package manifest before and after copying, creates a versioned directory under ~/.local/share/vesper-apps and preserves an existing launcher. Use --prefix with your own absolute directory to choose another installation location. Do not replace a running version.

sections.title: Linux launch and sandbox
sections.text: Launch the installed vesper-browser executable. The accepted Linux runtime used namespace and seccomp sandboxing. On the GPU-less qualification host, VESPER_GRAPHICS_BACKEND=software selected SwiftShader explicitly; this does not establish physical GPU compatibility or hide a software renderer. Do not disable the sandbox to imitate a passing check. Privileged Debian installation, AppImage and other architectures remain unqualified.

sections.title: Where your data lives
sections.text: Windows normally uses %APPDATA%/true-utopian/vesper. Linux uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/true-utopian/vesper, defaulting to ~/.local/share/true-utopian/vesper. An existing private ~/.vesper/desktop-location.json can select a canonical store. Explicit VESPER_DESKTOP_DATA_DIR overrides it. If a saved location is invalid, resolve it before launching; do not create an empty substitute and assume your profiles were lost. Uninstalling an application keeps its private data folders.

chapters.title: Your first Browser and Workbench run
chapters.description: Follow the local workflow from a profile to a saved archive.

sections.title: Open Browser
sections.text: Launch Vesper Browser and open Profiles. Create a profile with a descriptive name. Choose the engine and supported identity preset deliberately. A stock engine can browse normally; a Vesper native identity policy requires the qualified native kernel. Review the proxy and start pages before opening a profile. A fresh local installation does not contain another operator’s proxy credentials.

sections.title: Add Workbench
sections.text: Open Add-ons → Install Workbench. Select the signed .vesper-plugin.json manifest beside its matching .vplugin.tgz archive for Workbench 0.5.15. Review the reported version and permissions. Browser verifies its pinned signing key, package size and digest. Open Workbench from the new sidebar entry. Close standalone Workbench first: the standalone app and add-on share one Workbench store and cannot own it simultaneously.

sections.title: Run the owned example
sections.text: In Workbench, select New run and choose the bundled local fixture automation from the installed automation list. Use its local fixture destination and default inputs. Review the selected engine and profile policy, then submit once. Observe the run’s state in Runs & archives. If it awaits an operator action, use the matching input or finish control after inspecting the browser. Avoid substituting a third-party website for the owned example.

sections.title: Verify the result
sections.text: A completed website action is not sufficient: wait for the run to reach saved. Open its details, inspect the archive metadata and download the artifact. The saved record includes its digest and size. Keep that record with the file. A retained or failed run needs inspection and cleanup; do not delete its profile or repeatedly submit the same website action. The archive transport and run lifecycle guides explain the API equivalents.

sections.title: Finish normally
sections.text: Stop any manually opened profiles and use the tray menu’s Quit when finished. Closing the main window can leave the application in the tray and schedules running. After restart, confirm that the expected profiles, enabled Workbench add-on and saved runs are still visible. Scheduling requires the computer and Workbench service to remain running.

chapters.title: Updates, backups and recovery
chapters.description: Understand what an update verifies and what recovery still requires.

sections.title: Signed local updates
sections.text: App update, or Vesper → Install local update, opens a local .vesper-update.json manifest beside its installer. The shell checks the pinned Ed25519 key, product, platform, architecture, newer version, size and SHA-256. This local signature is separate from Windows Authenticode. There is no hosted automatic update feed or automatic rollback service in this release.

sections.title: Preserve the original store
sections.text: Finish active runs, resolve cleanup and stop profiles before replacing application files or selecting a changed engine. Use the guarded upgrade’s idle preflight and independently verified private backup. Keep original profiles, proxy vaults, tokens, signing trust and run history together. Copying a running database is not a verified backup. Never publish a backup, archive or its credentials.

sections.title: Changed native kernels
sections.text: An engine change needs native unit tests, direct and copied-runtime qualification, stopped and unleased profiles, plus a fresh verified backup before activation. Existing acceptance belongs to the exact executable and component hashes that were tested. A previous passing record does not qualify a changed binary. Standard users select a compiled runtime; building the kernel from source requires a separate large developer toolchain.

sections.title: Recovery limits
sections.text: Profile archives support compatible transport, but encrypted cookies are not guaranteed to work on another PC or after arbitrary browser downgrades. A complete application rollback and forced-exit recovery matrix remain unfinished. Retain the original store after an uncertain export or upgrade. Inspect the relevant run, lease and evidence before choosing a retry or explicit administrator interruption.

chapters.title: Build and contribute
chapters.description: Work on original source with an isolated development store.

sections.title: Choose the source project
sections.text: vesper-antidetect-browser is the independent Browser source repository. vesper-workbench contains the automation product and its Browser workspace dependency. Both are original projects by true-utopian under MIT. Preserve third-party notices. Keep vendor binaries, analysis traces, profiles, proxy lists, private keys and personal test results out of contributions.

sections.title: Source checks
sections.text: Workbench requires Node.js 26 or newer. Browser supports Node.js 24 or newer. From a clean checkout, install the locked dependencies, then run the source suite. These checks do not qualify an installed native runtime or a public binary release.

sections.title: Desktop development
sections.text: Use a dedicated VESPER_DESKTOP_DATA_DIR outside your normal private store. The Workbench repository provides desktop:workbench for shell iteration. Full Windows packaging needs its tested Chromium cache; Linux native runtime packaging must be performed on Linux. Build output remains local by default. Read the repository’s desktop and native qualification records before changing packaging or engine activation.

sections.title: Correct the documentation
sections.text: The wiki combines docs/handbook.json with the existing bundled API guides. scripts/build-public-docs.mjs generates the static site and Markdown wiki from those sources. Edit the source text, regenerate the output and run the documentation checks. Report the affected release and precise steps in an issue; omit access tokens, proxy credentials and private website content.
